CVE-2009-20005.title: InterSystems Caché UtilConfigHome.csp Stack Buffer Overflow
CVE-2009-20005.description: A stack-based buffer overflow exists in the UtilConfigHome.csp endpoint of InterSystems Caché 2009.1. The vulnerability is triggered by sending a specially crafted HTTP GET request containing an oversized argument to the .csp handler. Due to insufficient bounds checking, the input overflows a stack buffer, allowing an attacker to overwrite control structures and execute arbitrary code. It is unknown if this vulnerability was patched and an affected version range remains undefined.

CVE-2026-107240.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The /authenticate endpoint of this service passes user-supplied username and password values to child_process.exec() through a sanitizer (escapeRegExp) that removes regular expression metacharacters but not newline characters. An unauthenticated attacker can inject a newline character into the username field to execute arbitrary shell commands as the versa OS service user. No credentials are required; the attacker needs only a CSRF token, which can be obtained from an unauthenticated page load.

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

CVE-2026-120522.title: Cloud Storage Manager for Fluent Forms <= 1.2.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Write via Google Drive Filename Path Traversal
CVE-2026-120522.description: The Cloud Storage Manager for Fluent Forms – Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3 Uploads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.0. This is due to missing authorization checks on the `connection/{driver}/save` and `/download/single-file` REST endpoints, combined with insufficient path validation in the Google Drive `downloadFile()` function, where the Google Drive metadata `name` value is concatenated into a local path without `basename()`, `sanitize_file_name()`, or canonical path validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to store attacker-controlled Google Drive credentials, trigger a download of an attacker-owned file whose provider-returned filename contains path traversal, and write attacker-controlled content outside the intended `downloads` directory. When the written file has a PHP extension and lands in a web-accessible location, this can lead to remote code execution.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts.

CVE-2026-133276.title: Validation bypass of Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data
CVE-2026-133276.description: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

CVE-2026-135249.title: MISP Unauthenticated Decompression Bomb via Compressed Request Bodies
CVE-2026-135249.description:
MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed data. An unauthenticated attacker could send a small compressed payload that expands to a very large decompressed body, exhausting server memory and causing a denial of service. Brotli and zstd, with their high compression ratios, made the attack particularly effective.

The vulnerability required no authentication and no special conditions beyond the ability to send an HTTP request with a Content-Encoding header. The impact is a complete loss of availability for the affected MISP instance.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

CVE-2026-99453.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-blkfront: unbind irq before tearing down ring and shadow requests

In blkif_free_ring(), the driver tears down the ring's persistent grants,
shadow request arrays, and shared ring structure (xenbus_teardown_ring),
and only calls unbind_from_irqhandler() at the very end.

While blkif_free_ring() is freeing persistent grants and clearing the
shadow array, the event channel interrupt (blkif_interrupt) is still
registered and active. If an interrupt arrives from the backend during
this teardown window, blkif_interrupt() reads rinfo->ring.sring and,
via blkif_completion(), accesses rinfo->shadow[id].grants_used and
rinfo->shadow[id].sg. blkif_free_ring() tears these structures down
without holding rinfo->ring_lock, and the handler only checks
info->connected at entry, so this is a real race resulting in a
use-after-free or NULL pointer dereference.

Fix this by moving unbind_from_irqhandler() to the beginning…

CVE-2026-99527.title: spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference
CVE-2026-99527.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference

As noticed by Sashiko during a review run of an unrelated patch,
in of_spmi_register_devices(), for_each_available_child_of_node()
is used to loop through children, and to also assign a node to a
newly created SPMI child device.

Problem is that the refcount is dropped at every iteration so, in
the specific case of DT overlays, a use-after-free may occur when
an overlay is dynamically unloaded!

To resolve this, increase the of_node refcount when assigning (in
function of_spmi_register_devices) and release the reference in
spmi_device_remove().

CVE-2026-99592.title: x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes
CVE-2026-99592.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes

On AMD CPUs with INVLPGB, two live processes can get the same MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE
global ASID value. The two then hit each other's TLB entries, so each can read
or corrupt the other's memory.

The global ASID space is managed lazily. When a global ASID is freed, its bit is
set in the global_asid_freed bitmap. Once the free ASID search reaches the end
of the global_asid_used bitmap, a global flush is done to really reclaim the
lazily freed global ASIDs.

However, the current code can assign the same global ASID to two different
processes, if one process is assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE - 1, another process
MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, and both stick around (keeping their global ASID numbers in
use) until the search wraps around again. At that point a third process could
also get assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE.

the highest ASID stays in use, so it is not handed out…
